fields.meta_title: Exit Survey Builder With Reason Tracking | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an exit survey that sends when HR logs a resignation, codes each reason for leaving and splits results by team. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Exit Survey That Shows Why People Leave
fields.hero_description: Create an exit survey that reaches every leaver before the last day and shows HR which teams lose the people they meant to keep.
fields.features_heading: What an Exit Survey Has to Get Right
fields.features_subheading: An exit survey asks people on their way out what made them go and what might have kept them, in a form HR can count.
fields.feature_1:
Reasons from a fixed list

Opens with the primary reason for leaving, picked from a list you control, then a comment box. Fixed codes let HR count reasons across 200 exits, not reread 200 essays.
fields.feature_2:
Timed around the last day

Sends on a day you pick before the last day, while the details are still fresh, and closes on a date you set after departure. One reminder goes out if no answer has arrived.
fields.feature_3:
Confidential, with a team minimum

Shows HR every answer with the name attached. Managers see a team's results once it has five or more responses, and the comments they read arrive with names removed.
fields.feature_4:
Regretted exits counted apart

Pulls the regretted tag HR sets at offboarding. The dashboard then shows why the people you wanted to keep chose to go, kept apart from retirements and dismissals for cause.
fields.feature_5:
Splits from your HR records

Reads department and manager from your HRIS, such as BambooHR. Results split along those lines, and the survey never has to ask a leaver a single question about who they are.
fields.feature_6:
Your exit survey app, exported

Exports the whole app to your GitHub on paid plans, with its send rules, reason codes, and response database. Host it on your own servers or keep changing it in Emergent.

fields.usecase_heading: Exit Surveys for Four Kinds of Leavers
fields.tab_content_1:
A resignation in BambooHR sends the survey

When HR changes a status to Terminated with a resignation reason in BambooHR, the leaver gets 12 questions at the personal email on file, five days before the last day. One reminder follows two days later. Answers land in a table only HR can open, and the manager never sees them.
fields.tab_content_2:
Who wants to come back next summer

All 48 lifeguards and camp staff get an exit survey on their final shift, with one question the recruiter cares about most: would you work here next season? Anyone who answers yes and is marked eligible for rehire joins the May rehire list. This season, 31 of the 48 made the list.
fields.tab_content_3:
Support lost five people it wanted to keep

Over the last 12 months, each team's exits are tallied by reason and by the regretted tag. Support had seven leavers, five of them regretted, and four named manager support as the main reason. Because the team cleared the five-response minimum, its HR business partner got a direct message.
fields.tab_content_4:
Seniors grade their program before commencement

Seniors get the survey when they apply to graduate, and 289 of 412 answered this spring. Each program sees the share of its students who would recommend it. Biology came in lowest of three, with 41 of 71 saying yes, and its chair received the advising comments behind the score.

fields.howto_title: How to Run an Exit Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan an exit survey that leavers finish and HR can count, then build it in Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose between voluntary leavers only and everyone who leaves. People who were dismissed or laid off are answering a different question. Decide whether retirees and contract ends count too. Write the rule down, because someone will ask why one person got it and another did not.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A few days before the last day, the details are still fresh. Send the link to a personal address so it keeps working after the work account closes. Set one reminder and a closing date about two weeks after departure.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write eight to ten reasons for leaving, such as pay or manager support. Ask for one primary reason and one secondary. Add a single open question for detail. The list makes reasons countable, and the comments explain them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide whether HR reads each response with the name attached. Managers see team totals only above a minimum you set. Put both rules on the first screen in plain words, before anyone reaches question one.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write it the way you would brief a colleague, covering the audience, the timing, the reason list, and who sees what. Emergent builds the survey with its send rules, response table and HR dashboard. A later change takes one more message.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect BambooHR or any HRIS with an API. Department, manager and the regretted tag then come from HR records, not from the leaver. The survey stays short, and every split matches the org chart HR already keeps.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the reason counts once a quarter, not after each departure. Compare regretted exits by team and tenure, and look for a reason that keeps rising. Take one finding to the leadership meeting with the comments behind it, then check next quarter's numbers.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits between templates (SurveyMonkey, SmartSurvey, Lattice), question lists (Formbricks, Perceptyx), one university HR page and a Reddit thread on whether leavers should answer honestly. This page answers both sides: the leaver's questions about honesty and what to say, and HR's questions about what to ask. Then it shows the survey running as an app: triggered by the HRIS, sent to a personal inbox, coded by reason, split by team only above a reporting minimum, with a rehire list for seasonal staff and a senior exit survey for a university.

og.headline: Build an exit survey
og.alt: Build an exit survey with Emergent

chip_prompts: Write 12 exit survey questions for my company. Start with the main reason for leaving from a fixed list, then ask what would have kept them and whether they would come back.
When HR marks a resignation in BambooHR, email my exit survey to the leaver's personal address five days before their last day, with one reminder two days later.
Give my exit survey a fixed list of 10 reasons for leaving, such as pay, manager support, and career growth, and count the main reason by team each quarter.
Ask each seasonal leaver if they would work here next season, and put everyone who says yes and is eligible for rehire on a list for my recruiter.

scope.evidence: H1 "Build an Exit Survey That Shows Why People Leave"; hero "Create an exit survey that reaches every leaver before the last day and shows HR which teams lose the people they meant to keep." (D1 ok); how-to description one sentence (D2 ok).

intent.evidence: Serves both sides the top 10 shows: leaver questions (honesty, whether to fill it out) and HR questions (good questions, how many, templates, exit interview form, software, student version), plus a 7-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: HR vocabulary: "regretted tag HR sets at offboarding", "Terminated with a resignation reason in BambooHR", "five-response minimum", "eligible for rehire"; employee table variant used.

openers.evidence: "When HR changes a status to Terminated", "All 48 lifeguards and camp staff", "Over the last 12 months", "Seniors get the survey"; feature bodies open on verbs ("Opens", "Sends", "Shows", "Pulls", "Reads", "Exports").

craft.evidence: "Fixed codes let HR count reasons across 200 exits, not reread 200 essays." "Write the rule down, because someone will ask why one person got it and another did not." QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean.

voice.evidence: Operator detail ("Advising slots were booked three weeks out.", five days before the last day, one reminder two days later); no AI-tell vocabulary.

truth.evidence: BambooHR webhook, confidential vs anonymous, reporting minimum and regretted attrition all sourced; numbers agree: 31 of 48; Support 7 leavers, 5 regretted, 4 manager support; 289 of 412 = 70%; Biology 41 of 71 = 58%.

distinct.evidence: Owns departures (reasons, regretted exits, rehire list); links employee-engagement-survey and pulse-survey without taking their topics. Template overlap with onboarding-survey kept as a note.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first ("Yes, with care.", "Usually, yes.", "About 10 to 15."); hub link in item 2; two sibling links; F9 lines in items 6 and 9.

images.evidence: Tab 1 Jordan Ellis, survey 5 days before last day, HR only; tab 2 31 of 48 on the May rehire list; tab 3 Support 7/5 with DM to Dana Ruiz, Finance hidden under 5; tab 4 70% response, Biology 41 of 71. One hero each, readable.
